text:
All tests pass.

Root cause: `wait_exponential.__call__` used `exponent = retry_state.attempt_number` (which is 1 on the first retry), so the wait was `multiplier * exp_base**1` instead of `multiplier * exp_base**0`. This made every wait one power of `exp_base` too large, and since `wait_random_exponential` builds on this same computation, it inherited the same off-by-one error.

Fix: changed the exponent calculation to `retry_state.attempt_number - 1`, so the first retry waits `multiplier * exp_base**0 == multiplier` and each subsequent attempt multiplies by `exp_base`, matching the documented behavior.

final_text:
All tests pass.

Root cause: `wait_exponential.__call__` used `exponent = retry_state.attempt_number` (which is 1 on the first retry), so the wait was `multiplier * exp_base**1` instead of `multiplier * exp_base**0`. This made every wait one power of `exp_base` too large, and since `wait_random_exponential` builds on this same computation, it inherited the same off-by-one error.

Fix: changed the exponent calculation to `retry_state.attempt_number - 1`, so the first retry waits `multiplier * exp_base**0 == multiplier` and each subsequent attempt multiplies by `exp_base`, matching the documented behavior.
